acts.desc: Ira takes a flight with travel writer Ken Hegan, to witness Ken deploying a travel gadget that keeps the seat in front of him from reclining. This means more knee space for Ken — but does he get away with it, really?
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: A boy rides shotgun in a memorable car ride with his mother, and in the process learns how his father earns money for their family. This story appears in Domingo Martinez’s memoir, The Boy Kings of Texas, which was a finalist for the National Book Award. (17 min)
acts.title: Take Your Kid to Work Day

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: We asked listeners to call in with their stories of getting away with it, and got nearly 1000 messages. Here are a handful.
acts.title: Get Away With It After the Beep

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Molly Shannon tells the story of when she and a friend evaded a whole lot of adults to travel half-way across the country, despite the fact that they were twelve years old and wearing tutus. Her story was recorded during a live taping of WTF with Marc Maron.
acts.title: Crime and Tutus

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Producer Alex Blumberg tells the story of how Oklahoma, against huge odds, came to have the first and best publicly-funded pre-school system in the country, and how one businessman joined the fight because a cardboard box full of evidence convinced him that pre-school was the smartest business decision the state could make.
acts.title: Pre K-O
